logistic.png: S-shaped conversion curve. The same shift changes conversion more near the middle than near either end.
ml-flow.png: Machine learning workflow from data with known outcomes to predictions where outcomes are unknown.
model-fit.png: Simple, intermediate and complex models fitted to the same training observations.
model-opt.png: The customer population is partitioned by predicted net value to search for a coupon decision within each group.
non-linear-case.png: Nonlinear demand curves show how price sensitivity can vary with the price level as well as the weather.
non-linear.png: Example of nonlinear effects of covariates in the sales model.
normal_dist.jpeg: Normal distribution with about 95% of its probability within two standard deviations of the mean.
opt-deriv.png: Net value rises and then falls with coupon amount, with the best amount at the curve's maximum.
p_value.png: Tail areas under the null distribution illustrate how a p-value is calculated.
partitions.png: Prediction-based customer partitions used to compare coupon amounts within each band.
personalise.png: Customer segments for which different coupon amounts can maximize net value.
ps-experiment.png: Randomized email assignment using probabilities tailored to customer characteristics.
qob.png: School-entry and dropout rules show why quarter of birth can affect time spent in school.
rdd.png: Potential-outcome curves near a threshold, with observed data switching from control to treatment at the cutoff.
rdd_fuzzy.png: Fuzzy regression discontinuity: crossing the cutoff changes the probability of treatment without determining receipt.
regr_space.png: Matrix representation of synthetic control, with a weighted sum across control units used to predict the treated unit.
regr_space_x.png: Synthetic control matrix with additional predictors stacked alongside outcomes to fit the same set of unit weights.
regr_time.png: Matrix representation of a regression using indicators for each period.
s-learner.png: A single outcome model predicts both treatment choices. Their difference estimates the effect.
second-stage-x.png: Second-stage X-learner fit to imputed treatment effects, illustrating why the two group fits can differ.
slice-1.png: Slicing a peaked outcome curve by outcome level groups observations with opposite treatment-response slopes.
slice-2.png: Slicing a monotonic waiting-time response by outcome level groups observations with similar slopes.
synth_img.png: Treated and comparison series before intervention and the unobserved untreated trajectory of the treated unit after intervention.
t-learner-problem.png: Separate models fitted to unequal treatment groups can imply varying effects even when the true effect is constant.
t-learner.png: Separate outcome models are trained on treated and control groups. Their prediction difference estimates the effect.
t-vs-x-learner.png: Estimated treatment effects from the T-learner and X-learner compared in an example with unequal group sizes.
test.png: The same three fitted models evaluated on held-out observations, illustrating generalization beyond the training set.
translation.png: Prediction as a mapping between inputs and outputs, illustrated with language translation.
waiting-time.png: Contrasting response curves for coupon profitability and the effects of waiting for customer service.
x-learner.png: X-learner diagram showing outcome models, imputed effects, second-stage effect models and their weighted combination.
zero-bias-s-learner.png: Simulated true and S-learner estimated causal effects, illustrating shrinkage toward zero under regularization.
